title: rwb-access timer and case read: the authorise request attribute set, the label of the matrix version in force and the scope that prevails under an escalation are not specified
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 41 and 43; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1, T6.1 and T-A.1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 and A2.14; Legacy RWB-E1-028 sections 3, 10 and 12
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 and 5; section 5 Exception paths; section 7 Background; section 8 BR1, BR2, BR3 and BR4; section 11 Data; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Three values this slice needs are absent from every source. (1) The attribute set of an authorise request for a timer or case read: Architecture v5 slide 14 names POST /authorise with role, scope and DoA and TSD P4 T-A.1 lists no authorise path and no request schema, so the fields the caller sends for a timer read or a case read - the case, its queue, team and owner, the object asked about, the timer type and status, the escalation level, escalatedToRole and escalatedAt - are a read and not a source value. (2) The label of the matrix version in force at the 30 November 2026 release date: the FSD examples use PM-2026.12 and the load-path example moves from PM-2026.11 to PM-2026.12, but no source states which version is in force on the release date. (3) Which scope prevails, and which scope the answer names, when the caller's own or team scope and an escalation grant both admit the case.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access the cached authorise operation and slide 41 gives the first API path /authorise, while TSD P4 T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none of them is an authorise path and TSD P4 T3.1 defines no authorise request or answer object; FSD P4 A2.4 AC-P4-004-01 and AC-EXC-P4-004-02 use PM-2026.11 and PM-2026.12 as load examples without naming the version in force on a date; Legacy RWB-E1-028 AC2 says the breach goes to RW-TEAMMGR without saying which scope the role then reads the case under, and section 12 lists only the timer and case read endpoints.
proposed: Fix the authorise attribute set for a case read and a timer read in the API specification and TSD P4 T-A, with escalatedToRole and escalatedAt among the attributes; name the matrix version in force at the release date in the policy pack; and state that the answer names the scope of the escalation grant with the reason ESCALATED_TO_ROLE and reports no scope wider than the caller's role row carries.

title: Authority attributes, matrix version label and role roster for an allocation and queue read
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P4 Access and administration v3.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1.md; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 1 Story Files v7/RWB E1 020 Allocation and assignment engine v1 v2.md
description: Three values are missing for the authority slice of this key. First, the exact attribute set of an authorise request for an allocation, queue or summary read is not fixed by any source. Second, the label of the permission-matrix version in force at the release date of 30 November 2026 is not stated. Third, the roster of role codes that hold Queue and allocation letters in the matrix is not fixed.
evidence: FSD P4 A2.4 AC-P4-004-01 uses matrix version PM-2026.12 with validFrom 2026-12-01 and names RW-LEGAL and RW-CASEOWN letters only; FSD P4 A2.14 gives the scope rule but no roster; TSD P4 T6.1 has three columns (Rules and parameters, Reference data, Platform administration) and no Queue and allocation column, so it fixes no roster; legacy RWB-E1-020 section 10 names RW-TEAMMGR, RW-CASEOWN, RW-PLATADM, SY-CASEWF, SY-RULES and RW-REFADM without a letter per area, and its section 12 fixes no request shape.
proposed: Act on the defaults this story records: the request carries the area, the right, the team code and the business date for a summary read, and the case ID with its team and owner reference for a case read; PM-2026.11 is the version in force at the release date with PM-2026.12 approved from 2026-12-01; RW-TEAMMGR and RW-CAPACITY hold Queue and allocation R with scope TEAM, RW-CASEOWN holds R with scope OWN, RW-AUDIT holds R with scope ALL, SY-CASEWF holds CRU, SY-RULES holds R, RW-REFADM holds none and RW-PLATADM holds Platform administration U for a rerun.

title: The review-item authorise request shape, the label of the matrix and masking versions in force at the release date, and the review-field roster of the masking pack are fixed by no source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (rwb-access IN: POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions, /masking-policies; answer cached), slide 41 (P4 owns Recovery roles as data, scope, masking policy, access log), slide 43 (AccessPolicyChanged to all for cache refresh) and slide 44 (JOB-12 document intake and JOB-17 retention owned by rwb-document); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1, T3.2 LOV-SCOPE, T6.2 and appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.1, A2.4, A2.5, A2.7, A2.8, A2.14 and A2.30; Legacy RWB-E1-054 sections 3, 4, 7, 8 and 11; Ownership Map (document, document_intake, document_field, document_text, document_checklist_item owned by P5; lov_value by P3); Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 section R9
section: Section 1 Story; section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 to 8; section 7 AC1 to AC8; section 11 Data; section 12.1 and 12.8; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Three values a review-queue authority slice needs are absent from every source. (1) The attribute set of an authorise request for a review item. Architecture v5 slide 14 names POST /authorise with the parenthesised words role, scope, DoA and calls the answer cached, but neither Architecture v5 nor TSD P4 gives the request or the answer schema, and TSD P4 appendix T-A.2 defines only API-P4-012 GET /me/session. So the item reference, the review reason, the predicted type, the two candidates, the candidate cases with their team and region and the field IDs in REVIEW are carried by default, and the review team of an unattached item is carried in the request as well: the value is the REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED parameter of rwb-document, named DOC-SVC by the legacy assumption, and the parameter row is P5's, so this service may not read it (DP-01). (2) The label of the matrix and the masking versions in force at the release date of 30 November 2026. PM-2026.12 and MASK-SIT-01 are the labels used, but no source dates either version, no source states which version is in force on that date, and FSD P4 A2.5 names MASK-SIT-01 only as the version of a test case. (3) The roster of review-field IDs that masking_rule must cover. No source lists the field IDs of a review item or of a document whose fields are in REVIEW, FSD P4 A2.5 names no field roster at all, and FSD P4 A2.7 names DF-PTY-007, DF-PTY-008 and DF-PTY-016 for the case record view only. The story therefore answers a marker for whatever field IDs a request names and writes no roster in code. The acting defaults are carried by the three assumption rows; nothing here blocks the build, because every value is a row, a list value or an attribute of a request read at run time.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 14 reads REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) with no schema, and its note reads each service authorises the object itself using cached permission data from rwb-access; slide 41 gives /authorise as the first API path of the service. TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 and none of them is the authorise path; T-A.2 defines GET /me/session only; T3.1 defines role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit with columns but no request or answer shape; T3.2 lists LOV-SCOPE as OWN, TEAM, REGION and ALL with no attribute to match TEAM or REGION against. FSD P4 v3 A2.4 VR-P4-004-1 and A2.14 VR-P4-014-1 give the two messages and no field set; A2.5 AC-EXC-P4-004-05 names MASK-SIT-01 and v_ace_customer.date_of_birth and no review field; A2.7 AC-P4-007-01 names DF-PTY-007 and DF-PTY-016 marked masked for the case record view. Legacy RWB-E1-054 section 3 gives REVIEW_TEAM_UNATTACHED as DOC-SVC assumed, section 4 step 2 gives the queue rule, section 11 lists the document and intake fields P5 owns, and section 12 gives the authorization column as Documents right R or U with no request shape. No source dates PM-2026.12 or MASK-SIT-01 or fixes a review-field roster.
proposed: At the RWB-P5-E1054-CON and RWB-P4-E1037-CON reviews, publish the review-item authorise request and answer schema in the API specification and in TSD P4 appendix T-A, naming the review team attribute and every other attribute the request carries; record the matrix and masking version labels in force at each release date with their valid-from dates and their environment; and list the review-field IDs the masking pack must cover with the pack version, so that the three acting defaults of this story become source values and the placeholder disappears. Until then the story reads every value at run time, marks it with the R9 placeholder and writes no literal in code.

title: The authorise attribute set, the policy version labels and the full field-ID roster of the read-only case record view are fixed by no source
source: FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.11, A2.14; TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1 and T3.2; legacy RWB-E1-023 sections 4, 7, 10 and 11; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14, 41 and 43
description: Three values behind the read-only case record view are fixed by no source. First, the attribute set of an authorise request for the CASE_RECORD area: the legacy flow reads the case facts inside the module (legacy section 4 steps 2 to 7) and the target moves them into a one-hop request, but no source lists the attributes the request carries for a case-record read. Second, the label of the matrix version and of the masking version in force at the release date of 30 November 2026: the FSD names PM-2026.12, PM-2026.13 and MASK-SIT-01 as loads and examples and never says which of them is in force on that date. Third, the full roster of case-record personal field IDs: the legacy AC8 and the FSD exception AC-EXC-P4-004-05 name DF-PTY-007, DF-PTY-008 and DF-PTY-016 as examples, and no source gives the complete list of personal field IDs a case-record read marks.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-023 section 4 step 3 checks the right and the scope and step 7 fills each personal field through the masker without naming the request attributes; FSD P4 A2.11 A2.11.3.2 carries only role and permission columns, and A2.14 names the scope values but not the attributes compared; TSD P4 T3.1 gives permission.matrix_version and masking_rule.masking_version as free varchar(20) with no release-date row; legacy RWB-E1-023 section 11 lists the v_ace_customer and v_ace_contact fields one by one and never closes the roster of personal field IDs.
proposed: Take the acting default: the authorise request carries the case reference, the owner, the queue, the team, the region, the action the caller is about to take and the field IDs asked about, and nothing else; PM-2026.12 and MASK-SIT-01 are the versions in force at the release date and a later version reaches the answer only through rwb.access.AccessPolicyChanged.v1; the field IDs of this slice are DF-PTY-007, DF-PTY-008 and DF-PTY-016, and any other field ID is accepted as data and marked masked when no row covers it.

title: rwb-access transfer and legal hold: the authorise request attributes, the matrix version label in force at the release date and the role holding Queue and allocation U are not fixed by any source
source: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 (rwb-access IN line), 41 (service catalogue) and 43 (AccessPolicyChanged consumers); TSD P4 Access and administration v3 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1 and T-A.1; FSD P4 Access and administration v3 A2.4 AC-P4-004-01 and AC-ALT-P4-004-02, A2.7, A2.14 and A2.30; Legacy RWB-E1-021 sections 3, 10, 12 and 16
section: Section 3 Preconditions; section 4 Flow steps 2 and 4; section 7 Background and AC1 to AC7; section 8 Business rules BR2, BR3 and BR9; section 10 Authority; section 11 Data; section 13 Configuration and reference data
description: Three values this slice needs are absent or unresolved. (1) Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41 name POST /authorise the first API path of rwb-access, but TSD P4 appendix T-A.1 lists API-P4-004 to API-P4-021, none of them is the authorise path, and no request schema is defined, so the attributes a transfer or a hold request must carry - the case reference, the team, the owner, the action and legalHold - are a read, not a source value. (2) The label of the permission matrix version in force at the release date of 30 November 2026 is named nowhere: the FSD tests an approved load of PM-2026.12 with validFrom 2026-12-01 and the TSD holds matrix_version as a column only, so the story reads the label from permission.matrix_version and names no label in code. (3) Which role holds Queue and allocation letter U in the matrix as loaded is not tabulated: the legacy story names RW-TEAMMGR and RW-CAPACITY, and the TSD T6.1 RBAC matrix has no Queue and allocation column at all. The proposed value is the acting default: the request carries the case reference, the team, the owner, the action and legalHold; the matrix version is read from permission for the business date; and RW-TEAMMGR and RW-CAPACITY hold the letter U, as the legacy story says.
evidence: Arch v5 slide 14 OUT line of rwb-access reads REST POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA), GET /me/permissions and /masking-policies with no request schema; TSD P4 T-A.1 runs API-P4-004 to API-P4-021 with no authorise path, and T3.1 defines role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict, delegation_limit, lov_value and the four rule tables only; TSD P4 T6.1 tabulates Rules and parameters, Reference data and Platform administration only; FSD P4 AC-P4-004-01 loads PM-2026.12 with validFrom 2026-12-01 and names no version in force on the release date; Legacy RWB-E1-021 section 3 names RW-TEAMMGR and RW-CAPACITY for Queue and allocation U and section 12 fixes no request body.
proposed: Publish the authorise request and answer schema with its legalHold attribute in RWB-P4-E1037-CON and the API specification, confirm the matrix version label in force at the release date with the matrix owner, and tabulate the Queue and allocation letters in TSD P4 T6.1 before the matrix version goes in force.
